title: Proactive fallback regulator with stall-probing and multivariate trip logic
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Problem: Regional/tier overloads and transient capacity shortfalls are causing customer-visible 429s, p95/p99 latency spikes, and timeout errors. Existing hard thresholds flip fallbacks too eagerly or too late, leading to unnecessary model downgrades or customer errors.

Goal: Build a proactive fallback regulator that combines multi-signal scoring (rate-limits, error-rate, latency, timeout counts, and KV-cache miss bursts) with active stall-probing and a probation/decay model to: (1) reduce false-positive fallbacks, (2) expedite safe cutovers when a region/tier is degraded, and (3) select fallback model variants with minimal quality regression.

Scope: routing controller + runtime hooks + telemetry + console dashboards + rollout plan. Not in scope: model training or new model variants beyond curated candidates already in the catalog.
acceptance_criteria: A multivariate trip score computed per region-tier-route that combines short-window 429/sec spikes, rolling p99 latency, timeout rate, and error-rate into a single normalized signal
Stall-probe subsystem executes synthetic probes (warm KV cache, small-batch inference) with probabilistic quorum to validate degraded status before opening a long-lived circuit
Circuit states implemented: CLOSED, PROBING, OPEN, COOLDOWN with configurable decay windows per-customer and per-tier

Fallback variant selector integrates with model-compatibility matrix and prefers lowest-cost candidate that passes safety checks (tokenization compatibility, function-calling parity, schema mapping), with an automatic revert if quality regressions detected by eval-set metrics
Instrumentation and dashboards in Redwood Console: trip-score heatmap, probe success ratio, per-tenant probation timers, and rollback triggers
Canary rollout and rollback automation: feature-gated, 10% tenant canary, automatic rollback on eval regression or customer-impact > medium

implementation_notes: Trip score normalization: use per-route baseline distributions (rolling 24h) to compute z-scores; fall back to global baseline for new routes.
Stall-probing: probes run from 3 distinct AZs per region, use warmed KV cache path and low token limit (<=32). Probe quorum = majority pass within probe window (30s).
Backoff schedule: probe frequency doubles each failed open cycle up to 30m; cooldown uses exponential decay per-tenant with initial half-life 6m.
Fallback variant selection: consult model_compat matrix in Catalog service; prefer quantized variant with latency < target and tracked eval delta < 3% on key prompts.
Per-tenant hysteresis: probation windows are tracked per-tenant; tenants on Dedicated get more conservative thresholds by default.
Telemetry: emit trip_score, probe_result, circuit_state, fallback_variant, and tenant_probation_timer as tags for tracing and metric aggregation.
Operational limits: safeguard to never globally open circuits for >5% of total requests without manual approval in Console. This prevents mass silent downgrades.
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Probes might themselves be rate-limited or skewed by cold caches. Mitigation: use warmed path and quota-exempt probe tokens; fall back to a secondary probe that uses a small warmup request sequence.
Risk: Mis-calibrated weights could cause oscillation between variants. Mitigation: conservative defaults, circuit hysteresis, and short PROBING windows with immediate revert if eval-set degrades.
Risk: Per-tenant decay could allow a slow attacker to force repeated cutovers. Mitigation: require minimum signal strength and set maximum per-tenant fallback frequency per hour.
Risk: Too many simultaneous fallbacks increases load on lower tiers. Mitigation: implement global admission cap and staggered rollouts across regions.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 - Lab: unit + integration tests + simulated workload replay (3 days)
Phase 1 - Canary: 10% of tenants, monitor trip_score and eval-set for 48h, automatic rollback on regression >0.05 R@K or customer-impact > medium
Phase 2 - Regional ramp: expand per-region at 30% increments over 7 days if metrics stable
Phase 3 - Global: enable by default with conservative thresholds, continue A/B tuning for weights and probe quorum
follow_ups: Add automated weight tuning job that uses reinforcement learning on historical incidents (future ticket)
Expose per-route tuning knobs in Console for enterprise customers (feature request)
Post-release: run a 30-day analysis to compare unit-cost delta and customer-visible errors vs baseline
